architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept quantitative transfer of H-CORE to the E2 core if the replicate-mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to agreement with the 9.51% prediction within the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-CORE for transfer to the E2 core if the replicate-mean SI_15_60 is below 7.51%, more than 2.00 percentage points below its 9.51% prediction. A value below 4.755% is additionally in the registered low-drift regime, but it does not support or falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL because this candidate contains neither modifier axis. A value above 11.51% rejects numerical agreement with the H-CORE prediction in the high-drift direction but does not adjudicate H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the supplied Skeptic/Robustness matched E2-core modifier contrast using M-HOLD-120: acrylic-only versus the same acrylic loading plus a non-zero minor tackifier, with a core-only control and preferably a tackifier-only arm. Preserve E2 core ratios, use at least two independently prepared repeats per arm, and fix and record preparation and thermal history. Exact catalog candidate IDs for this contrast were not supplied.

Among the tied supplied cards, S1C02 minimizes composition extrapolation by exactly matching the E2 anchor.

I did not adopt the Robustness Adjudicator's preferred multi-arm replacement as the committed card because no exact candidate ID or complete catalog experiment card for that contrast was supplied.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C, with hold stability not yet measured for the E2-anchored local candidate design.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run measured SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 C; even the best original reference, E1, increased by 9.51% over the same window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only one measured 120 C hold trajectory is available for each of E1 and E5, with four points over 15-90 min, and no thermal-hold trajectory is available for E2 or any candidate composition. In contrast, temperature response was measured from 80 to 130 C for multiple formulations and runs, while realized viscosity-level variability is directly documented for E2 despite its large spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 without extrapolation.
Run at least two independent repeats per tested composition so the matched-window drift can be compared against the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.

Include compositions that separate the registered mechanisms: a reactive-core-only reference, an acrylic-only modification, and a composition with both acrylic-like and non-zero minor tackifier-like axes.

For each composition, calculate the preregistered H-CORE prediction E1_drift multiplied by reactive mass fraction and compare the measured drift with both the linear prediction and the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that prediction.
Record and control preparation and thermal history so between-preparation state displacement is not mistaken for formulation-driven drift suppression.

Measure or anchor the realized viscosity level within the existing 80-130 C support so a drift result is interpreted alongside the actual starting rheological state rather than nominal composition alone.
Preserve the same 15-60 min comparison window and 120 C hold temperature across references and candidates.
planner.scientific_question: At matched 120 C hold conditions, do resin-modified E2-core compositions suppress SI_15_60 substantially below the reactive-mass linear-dilution prediction, and can an acrylic-only composition reach the low-drift regime without a non-zero minor tackifier fraction? The outcome must distinguish reactive-core dilution (H-CORE) from superlinear resin suppression (H-RESIN) and test the tackifier requirement asserted by H-DUAL.

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE versus H-RESIN: no resin modifier is present, so superlinear resin suppression cannot be attributed or tested
H-CORE versus H-DUAL: neither modifier axis is active, so tackifier requirement cannot be tested
H-RESIN versus H-DUAL: their predictions coincide for this unmodified composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two repeats would be more than 2 percentage points below the 9.51% H-CORE prediction and would therefore falsify H-CORE for the E2 core. Because this formulation contains no resin modifier, that result would not by itself establish H-RESIN or falsify H-DUAL; it would instead show that the E1-derived linear-core prediction is not transferable to E2.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result near 9.51% within the 2 percentage-point resolution would support H-CORE for the E2 baseline. A result substantially above 9.51% would show greater core drift than predicted rather than cleanly support the linear rule. In either case, the absence of both modifier axes prevents adjudication of H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: Drift between 4.75% and 9.51% would indicate partial suppression relative to the reference prediction but would not meet the preregistered H-RESIN low-drift threshold. If the deviation from 9.51% exceeds 2 percentage points it would challenge H-CORE, but no resin mechanism could be assigned from this core-only experiment.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode over the matched 15-60 minute window with no regression, extrapolation, or imputation. S1C02 is the exact, locally characterized E2 core and therefore provides the most interpretable baseline within the reported top tie. Its limitation is explicit: as a core-only card, it separates none of the registered mechanism pairs and cannot answer whether acrylic-only or dual-axis resin modification produces superlinear suppression. Preparation and thermal history should therefore be tightly controlled during the required independent repeats because the measurement plan itself does not control the documented E2 process-state risk.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All nine cards have the identical VOI component vector and none separates a registered hypothesis pair. S1C02 is preferred because its normalized composition exactly matches the characterized E2 reactive-core anchor, the geometric center of the original local design, whereas the other tied candidates alter stoichiometry, polyol balance, or use interpolated cores. This gives the cleanest directly measured E2 baseline for subsequent matched modifier contrasts without additional composition extrapolation.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the single S1C02 core-only run with the Skeptic's matched contrast set while retaining S1C02 as the core-only control. Hold the E2 reactive-core ratios fixed; compare core-only, acrylic-only, and acrylic plus non-zero minor tackifier at matched acrylic loading, preferably with a tackifier-only arm. No catalog candidate ID for this complete set is supplied, so the preferred_candidate_id is descriptive rather than an existing card identifier.
residual_decision_risk: The supplied payload withholds all quantitative decision-stability outputs, so recommendation-flip boundaries and the margin to the first strictly lower experiment cannot be evaluated.
No exact candidate ID or full composition for the required matched modifier contrast set is supplied.

M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state, while E2 showed up to a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C; preparation and thermal history must be operationally fixed, recorded, and handled consistently across arms.
The acrylic-like and minor-tackifier external-prior queries returned no rows, so local modifier choices remain supported only by the candidate-space analogue summary and its stated claim boundaries.
If either modifier contains reactive functionality, true NCO:OH stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.
At least two independently prepared repeats per composition, predefined replicate aggregation, and disagreement handling are still required to apply the 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
A three-arm design without a tackifier-only arm will not fully isolate main effects and interaction as cleanly as the preferred 2x2 modifier design.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The objection is decisive for experiment selection, not merely interpretation. S1C02 activates neither modifier axis and gives identical 9.51% predictions for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, with zero pairwise separation. It can test only transfer of the E1-derived H-CORE baseline to the E2 core. The stated scientific question instead requires a matched E2-core contrast including core-only, acrylic-only, and acrylic plus non-zero minor tackifier formulations; a tackifier-only arm would further complete the preferred 2x2 design. All arms should use M-HOLD-120 under explicitly fixed and recorded preparation and thermal history.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is within the disclosed nine-card tied top set, although S1C01::M-HOLD-120 is first in policy order. The decision-stability report is withheld and supplies no top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, or recommendation_flip_boundary values, so no specific weight perturbation or flip threshold can be identified. Scientifically, re-weighting hypothesis_discrimination and decision relevance above minimal perturbation size would be defensible because every disclosed top card separates zero registered hypothesis pairs and therefore cannot answer the stated resin-mechanism question.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can directly produce an SI_15_60 value below 4.75%, which would operationally challenge the E1-derived H-CORE prediction by more than the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. It can also numerically produce a value at or above 9.51%. However, the full stated criterion is not scientifically attainable for this composition: no result can validly falsify H-RESIN without a resin-modified formulation, and no result can falsify H-DUAL through an acrylic-only condition when AC1920 is 0.0%. Thus only the H-CORE baseline-transfer criterion is attainable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be misrepresented as adjudicating the registered resin mechanisms when it only measures the E2 core baseline and tests transferability of the E1-derived 9.51% prediction.
objections.objection: The selected experiment S1C02::M-HOLD-120 activates neither modifier axis: AC1920 = 0.0 wt% and TK100 = 0.0 wt%. Its registered predictions are identical at 9.51% for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, so every pair has 0.00 percentage-point separation, below the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. It therefore cannot deliver the scientific_question requirement to distinguish H-CORE from H-RESIN or test the tackifier requirement in H-DUAL. The proposer correctly declares all three pairs unseparated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A deviation from 9.51% could reflect realization or preparation state rather than failure of the E1-derived H-CORE prediction. Acrylic, tackifier, and joint modifier mechanism attributions remain entirely unavailable because both modifier axes are fixed at zero.
objections.objection: There is no modifier-axis composition confounding because neither axis moves. However, M-HOLD-120 has controls_process_state = false, the experiment card reports six missing process fields and process_state_risk = 0.75, and E2 previously showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C. The prose says preparation and thermal history should be tightly controlled, but the specified protocol only says to hold at 120 C and run two independent repeats; it does not operationally define or randomize the relevant process history.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: None for direct readout interpretation; the limitations arise from hypothesis coverage and process-state control rather than from model dependence.
objections.objection: No material interpretability defect is present in the primary observable. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C, with no fit, extrapolation, or imputation. The intermediate 30 and 45 min readings are not required for the primary calculation but provide a trajectory check.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Numerically possible outcomes would be assigned as falsifying or accepting H-RESIN and H-DUAL even though the required interventions are absent. At most, the experiment can challenge or support transfer of the H-CORE baseline prediction to E2.
objections.objection: Only the H-CORE portion of the stated criterion is practically attainable and applicable: SI_15_60 below 4.75% is 4.76 percentage points below the 9.51% prediction, exceeding the 2.00-point resolution. The other criterion clauses are invalid for this formulation. H-RESIN is defined for a resin-modified composition, but S1C02 contains no resin, so drift at or above 9.51% cannot falsify H-RESIN. H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only composition without tackifier, but S1C02 has AC1920 = 0.0%; the card incorrectly calls it 'this acrylic-only composition.' The acceptance criterion likewise incorrectly says that drift below 4.75% 'accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.'

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A core-specific rheological result could be overinterpreted as evidence for a resin mechanism that was neither instantiated nor measured.
objections.objection: No reliance on a hidden validation identity or unmeasured hold result is evident. The scope problem is instead the VOI card's mechanistic language: its acceptance criterion claims that a low-drift result in an unmodified core 'accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.' Rheology on a formulation containing no resin cannot establish resin-mediated dilution, reduced encounter frequency, or modifier specialization. The proposer's outcome_interpretation correctly narrows this to non-transferability of the E1-derived prediction, but that correction conflicts with the experiment card.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single core-only experiment with a matched contrast set using the same E2 reactive-core ratios and M-HOLD-120 protocol: core-only, acrylic-only, and acrylic plus non-zero minor tackifier. Hold acrylic loading constant between the latter two, calculate each formulation's preregistered E1_drift multiplied by reactive mass fraction, and preferably add a tackifier-only arm to form a 2x2 modifier design. Use at least two independently prepared repeats per composition under an explicitly fixed and recorded preparation and thermal-history protocol, and predefine replicate aggregation and disagreement handling. Retain the direct 15-60 min SI observable and the 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 has identical 9.51% predictions for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL and activates neither registered modifier axis, so it separates zero hypothesis pairs and cannot answer the stated scientific question.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream material-state structure, shared thermal-response evidence, state-calibration rules, and E1/E5 hold contrast before any candidate or experiment comparison is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: The candidate-space hypothesis and E2 reactive-core anchor are needed to identify admissible core-only, acrylic-only, and dual-axis experiments without treating candidate order as rank.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: The E2 composition fractions are needed to define the reactive-core anchor and calculate transparent reactive-mass fractions for linear-dilution predictions.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete measured E1 trajectory is needed as the least-drifting original reference and as the quantitative basis for H-CORE linear-dilution predictions.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete high-drift original trajectory is needed to characterize the observed failure-mode scale using the same matched time window.

tool_trace.name: get_repeatability_risk
tool_trace.reason: E2 shows approximately 2.80-3.57-fold run spread across the measured temperature range, so its realization uncertainty must be quantified before nominal viscosity is treated as a formulation property.

tool_trace.name: get_temperature_support
tool_trace.reason: Measured support and temperature-response summaries are needed to keep any viscosity-level anchor within the locally observed range and avoid unsupported extrapolation.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no acrylic-like entries, so source-level analogue evidence and its limitations are needed before choosing among sparsely covered acrylic-axis experiments.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no minor-tackifier entries, so source-level evidence is needed to assess the prior basis for experiments testing the tackifier requirement in H-DUAL.

voi_sent_to_model.note: The deterministic decision policy for this run is the stated rule ORDER. Experiments are presented in that order. Component vectors are unchanged facts.
voi_sent_to_model.order_description: perturbation size is minimized before intervention sufficiency is assessed

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
